title: Billing Standard: Balance Billed Back on an Early Payoff of Payment Arrangements
content:
**Billing standard — Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements): the balance billed back on an early payoff**

*The unbilled balance.* The unbilled balance is the amount moved into the agreement less every installment billed and every amount already billed back, as the agreement's ledger records them: the balance-transfer entries, less the installment-billed entries, less the billed-back entries.

*Arrears covered first.* Before any credit reduces the payoff, nothing on the account is covered first.

*Credits considered.* The credits considered are the bill credits posted to the service account in the month ending on the payoff day.

*Credits applied.* No credit standing on the service account is applied to the payoff.

*The balance billed back.* The balance billed back is the unbilled balance less the part of the credits applied that remains after the arrears covered first. The credits applied go first against the arrears covered first; only what is left of them after those arrears, never less than zero, is deducted from the unbilled balance. The result is never below zero and is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Worked figure (hypothetical ledger)**

| Ledger entries of the agreement | Amount |
|---|---|
| balance transfer at acceptance | $600.00 |
| installments billed (two of $150.00) | $300.00 |
| amounts already billed back | $0.00 |
| unbilled balance | $300.00 |

With nothing covered first and no credit applied, the balance billed back on the payoff day is $300.00.
